title: ROUTERS Act
official_title: To direct the Secretary of Commerce, acting through the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information, to conduct a study of the national security risks posed by consumer routers, modems, and devices that combine a modem and router, and for other purposes.
summary: The ROUTERS Act directs the Department of Commerce to study the national security risks posed by consumer routers, modems, and combined modem-router devices that are designed, developed, manufactured, or supplied by entities owned or controlled by China, Iran, North Korea, or Russia. Commerce must report findings to Congress within one year.
brief: Requires a Commerce Department national security study on consumer networking equipment made by entities linked to China, Iran, North Korea, or Russia, with a congressional report due within one year.

top_lines.headline: National Security Study on Foreign-Linked Routers
subs: Commerce must study national security risks from consumer routers, modems, and combined modem-router devices made by entities owned, controlled by, or subject to the influence of China, Iran, North Korea, or Russia
Report to Congress due within 1 year of enactment covering the study results

likelihoodReason: The bill passed the House and was received in the Senate in April 2025. The national security framing around Chinese networking equipment has bipartisan support in both chambers. However, with only 1 cosponsor in the House and no visible Senate companion, floor time may be limited. The 60-vote threshold and the fact that this is a study bill rather than a direct regulatory requirement may reduce opposition but also reduce urgency.

items.main: Names the Act the “Removing Our Unsecure Technologies to Ensure Reliability and Security Act” (the “ROUTERS Act”).
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Study of National Security Risks Posed by Certain Routers and Modems

items.main: Directs the Secretary of Commerce, acting through the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information, to study national security risks from consumer routers, modems, and combined modem-router devices made by entities owned, controlled, or subject to the influence of a covered country.
items.detail: The covered countries are those specified in section 4872(d)(2) of title 10, United States Code. Commerce must submit a report to the House Energy and Commerce Committee and the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee within one year of enactment. The bill does not prescribe the contents of the study, restrict the sale of covered devices, or authorize any regulatory action.

gaps: The bill directs a study but does not require Commerce to include any specific findings in the report, recommend any regulatory action, or propose a timeline for follow-on policy action based on the study results.

The bill covers consumer routers and modems but does not address enterprise or carrier-grade networking equipment from the same covered countries, which may present equal or greater national security risk.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Latta
featured_quotes.text: Routers and modems play a key role in communications networks. They are the entry point through which the public accesses the internet. Thus, we make sure that they are secure. Bad actors can exploit vulnerabilities in routers to infect users' computers, access their information, or disrupt their network.

added: Requirement for Commerce Department national security study on consumer routers, modems, and combined modem-router devices from entities linked to China, Iran, North Korea, or Russia
Congressional report due within one year of enactment
New subsection (c) requires the Secretary to consult with appropriate bureaus and offices within the Department of Commerce when conducting the study
modified: Study scope broadened to cover "national security risks and cybersecurity vulnerabilities" (was national security risks only)
"Covered country" cross-reference updated from section 4872(d)(2) to section 4872(f)(2) of title 10, U.S. Code
Section 2 heading shortened to "Study of Risks Posed by Certain Routers and Modems" (dropped "National Security")
